scope: Read-only static process-ownership review; no child processes, tests or supervisor execution by reviewer.
status: Concrete changes requested before acceptance; final delta review pending

findings.issue: Cancellation after the normal-exit observation but before owned cleanup finishes is recorded in cancellation_signal without changing exited status, so CLI can return success.
findings.requested_change: After cleanup, recheck cancellation before permitting normal exited success; preserve cleanup failure precedence.
findings.test: Inject cancellation after normal exit is observed and during cleanup; require non-success status even with checker returncode zero.

findings.issue: The bounded own_children read happens before signaling the still-unreaped known checker; procfs/count failures can return without stopping even that owned checker group. Failure is reported honestly, but known authority is left unused.
findings.requested_change: Attempt signal_owned(checker_pid) before enumerating descendants, retaining non-reaping proof and explicit failure handling.
findings.test: With known child ownership and an enumeration bound/error, verify known checker signal is attempted before returning cleanup_error.

findings.issue: A saved checker_pid is still used to classify later reaps after its original process has been reaped. Numeric reuse can overwrite the original checker returncode and miscount a later adopted child. No stale number is currently used as signaling authority, but identity classification should stop at first reap.
findings.requested_change: Track whether the original checker is already reaped and classify any later reap as a descendant even if its numeric PID matches.
findings.test: Synthetic reap stream with original checker completion followed by a later owned child carrying the same number must retain original checker exit and increment descendant count.

sound_paths: Each signal_owned call uses waitid WNOWAIT with one waiter before kill; a child exiting in between remains unreaped and reserves its PID.
Cleanup signals all currently observed children before the reaping phase and re-enumerates adoption on subsequent iterations; it does not use stored reaped PIDs for later signals.
Success requires no proc children plus ECHILD from P_ALL; descendant reaps on a normal exit become surviving_descendants failure.
Count/byte/reap/deadline failures are explicit cleanup_error, never Released or fallback.
Output is bounded jointly across both pipes; inherited pipe holders remain part of cleanup and post-reap EOF checking.
limitations: Process-group isolation follows the sole start_new_session checker lineage; no arbitrary external PID scan is used.
Finite cleanup cannot prove SIGKILL completion for unkillable kernel state; unresolved cleanup is explicitly failed.
